subject: EdgeFin benchmark methodology and SLO targets
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@edgefin.com>, Tomas Berg <tomas.berg@edgefin.com>
Cc: dylan.brooks@redwood.inference, dev.patel@redwood.inference
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: EdgeFin benchmark methodology and SLO targets

Thanks again for the time this morning — great conversation. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can align on a reproducible benchmark run.

Recap from today's discovery:
- Primary SLOs: latency and reliability for interactive chat and streaming use cases.
- Workload shape: mix of short assistant turns (~50–150 tokens) and longer completions for document generation (~500–2k tokens).
- Integration: streaming responses are used in product for progressive render; time-to-first-byte is important.

What we'd like to confirm from you:
1) Concrete latency targets (p50/p95/p99) and whether targets differ by request class (short chat vs long generative).
2) Throughput and concurrency targets (requests/sec and concurrent in-flight sessions).
3) Any constraints on tokenization or max sequence length we should enforce.
4) A sample of your prompt set + "gold" answers or eval criteria so we can compute quality/regression metrics.

What Redwood will provide for the benchmark:
- Our benchmark harness (attached) that drives both streaming and non-streaming workloads; it records token-level timings, time-to-first-byte, and per-request traces.
- A reproducible script and raw logs, plus a short report with p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput by client concurrency, and comparison vs your targets.

Attachments: (Attachment: redwood-benchmark-harness-v1.zip - zip) (Attachment: EdgeFin-MAP-20260815.pdf - pdf)

Proposed next step: you share the prompt set + gold answers; we run an initial benchmark in our Dedicated environment next week and share results + raw logs. If that sounds good, please confirm the target numbers and preferred test window.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@edgefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: Tomas Berg <tomas.berg@edgefin.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeFin benchmark methodology and SLO targets

Marissa — thanks for the recap and the harness. A few specifics from our side so you can scope the run:

Targets (by request class):
- Short interactive turns (typical chat): target p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 450ms for responses up to ~256 tokens.
- Long generation (document summarize/expand): target p95 <= 1200ms for responses ~1k tokens.
- Streaming: time-to-first-byte (TTFB) target <= 120ms for short turns.

Throughput/concurrency:
- Sustained throughput target: 250 req/s at peak traffic (mixed request types).
- Expected concurrency: up to 40 concurrent sessions (we define session as an active open connection sending/receiving streaming tokens).

Measurement notes:
- Please measure latencies at the application layer (end-to-end excluding client rendering), and include a breakdown of network vs model-side where possible.
- For streaming we care about TTFB and per-token inter-arrival median + 95th.

Attached is our prompt set and a small sample of "gold" expected outputs for quality checks. The prompt file is relatively small (~500 seeds) but representative. We also dropped a folder with a few production traces (anonymized) in the Drive link below to help reproduce your load shape.

Attachments: (Attachment: edgefin-prompt-set-v3.json - json)
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/edgefin-bench-2026
HubSpot: https://hubspot.company/objects/deals/EF-2026-0894

Questions for you:
- Can Redwood run the harness inside a Dedicated pool so we can see performance on reserved capacity?
- Will you be able to include token-level timings and raw server-side traces in the deliverable?

Best,
Priya
Head of Platform Engineering
EdgeFin
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@edgefin.com>, Tomas Berg <tomas.berg@edgefin.com>
Cc: dylan.brooks@redwood.inference, dev.patel@redwood.inference
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeFin benchmark methodology and SLO targets

Thanks Priya — that's very helpful. Quick clarifications so our run is reproducible and matches your expectations:

Measurement definitions we plan to use (please confirm):
- p95/p99 latency: measured from request start to response complete at the Redwood client harness; we will include a separate column removing network egress to isolate model-side time when your anonymized traces allow us to attribute.
- TTFB (streaming): time from request start to first token delivered to client.
- Per-token inter-arrival: median and p95 across streamed tokens.

Benchmark configuration items for confirmation:
- Prompt set: your edgefin-prompt-set-v3.json (~500 seeds) — we'll run with deterministic seeds and 3 iterations per seed to reduce variance unless you prefer a larger sample.
- Gold answers: please confirm the gold answer file format (JSONL?) and whether fuzzy-match scoring is acceptable for subjective tasks.
- Environment: we can run the harness in a Dedicated pool; we'll also run a quick hosted baseline for comparison.

Operational ask: for Dedicated runs we need a test API key and a small allowlist (or a one-time test VM) so the harness can exercise the exact serving path. If you prefer, we can run the harness in our Dedicated region and share a temporary endpoint for you to call.

Proposed schedule:
- Share final prompt set + gold answers by EOD Mon (Aug 17).
- Redwood runs Dedicated benchmark Tue (Aug 18) and shares raw logs + report Wed (Aug 19).

I'll loop in Dylan (cc) to coordinate the run.

-Marissa
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@edgefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: Tomas Berg <tomas.berg@edgefin.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 11:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeFin benchmark methodology and SLO targets

Marissa — confirmed. A few specifics to lock down:

Prompt set: attached as edgefin-prompt-set-v3.json (JSONL, 512–1024 token contexts for long cases). We also included a small "gold_answers.jsonl" file with expected outputs and a pass/fail rubric for deterministic tasks. For subjective tasks we accept BLEU/ROUGE style thresholds; please flag any evaluation mismatch so we can align.

Measurement clarifications:
- p95/p99: measure at the harness client after TCP handshake (i.e., include server processing but exclude client-side rendering).
- For reproducibility we use fixed RNG seeds; please honor the seed values embedded in the prompt file.
- Concurrency: count as simultaneous open requests to the model endpoint.

Access: we created a test API key scoped to a sandbox Dedicated pool; details are in Drive (edgefin-bench-credentials.txt). Key is valid for 48 hours starting Tue Aug 18 00:00 PT.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/edgefin-bench-2026 (contains prompt set, gold answers, sample traces, and the credential file)

Let us know if you need a formal NDA/PSA — legal is on standby.

Thanks,
Priya

Priya — thanks for the prompt set and the sandbox key. We'll prioritize a Dedicated run on Tue Aug 18. Quick operational notes:
- We'll run the harness with the fixed seeds you provided and 3 iterations per seed.
- Test window: Tue Aug 18, 02:00–06:00 PT (low production traffic). Please confirm if that window is acceptable.
- We'll capture token-level timings, TTFB, and per-request traces and upload raw logs to the shared Drive.
- Expect an initial README with commands to reproduce exactly the run and a tarball of raw traces.

Action items for Priya/Tomas: confirm the test window and verify the sandbox key is in the Drive and accessible to dylan_brooks@redwood.inference.

Subject: Re: EdgeFin benchmark methodology and SLO targets — Next steps

All — great progress. Finalizing next steps here so we're aligned:

1) Test window: Aug 18, 02:00–06:00 PT (Dedicated pool). Priya confirmed key is live and accessible.
2) Run config: edgefin-prompt-set-v3.json, fixed RNG seeds, 3 iterations per seed, mix of short/long request classes, up to 40 concurrent sessions to match your concurrency profile.
3) Deliverables: reproducible run script, raw token-level logs, summarized report with p50/p95/p99, TTFB numbers, throughput curves, and any quality regressions flagged against the gold answers.
4) Delivery ETA: initial report + raw logs by Wed Aug 19 EOD PT. We'll include a short appendix on measurement definitions and a reproducibility README.

Attachments: (Attachment: EdgeFin-MAP-20260815.pdf - pdf)

If anything changes to the key/window please flag immediately; otherwise we kick off the run tonight and report back tomorrow.

Appreciate the collaboration — looking forward to the results.

Cheers,
